title: Disaster assistance stages make administrative reach visible without proving payment, adequacy, or housing recovery
source_unit: OpenFEMA Registration Intake and Individuals Household Program aggregate snapshot for Los Angeles County wildfire disaster 4856
geography: Los Angeles County, California; 2025 wildfires and FEMA disaster 4856

observations.period: Current API snapshot retrieved September 19, 2026; aggregate city/ZIP program-stage rows

denominator.unit: city/ZIP rows in the OpenFEMA Registration Intake and Individuals Household Program dataset; aggregate categories are not a unique-survivor longitudinal denominator

valid_registrations.unit: valid registrations reported in the aggregate snapshot

ihp_referrals.unit: IHP referrals; 37.7069% descriptive ratio to valid registrations

ihp_eligible.unit: IHP-eligible records; 35.7154% descriptive ratio to referrals

reported_ihp_amount.unit: U.S. dollars in reported aggregate IHP amounts across housing-assistance and other-needs-assistance fields

receipt_and_recovery.unit: missing individual award issuance, payment date and receipt, amount adequacy, appeal, repair or housing completion, insurance interaction, stable placement, repeat crisis, trust, and later action

mechanism.value: Registration, referral, eligibility, and aggregate amount stages make administrative reach visible while leaving the practical gap between program status, usable payment, adequate recovery, and stable housing with survivors and unmeasured

observations.method: Structured extraction from the retained OpenFEMA API snapshot; aggregate stage counts and descriptive ratios are kept separate from person-level funnel, payment receipt, and housing recovery claims.
observations.uncertainty: The snapshot contains aggregate city/ZIP rows and stage-specific categories, not unique applicants followed over time. It does not disclose applicant identity, damage severity, application sequence, duplicate or invalid-record handling, appeal, payment issuance, receipt, or adequacy.
observations.subgroup: Los Angeles County wildfire registration and program-stage aggregates across 267 cities and 347 ZIP codes; no survivor-level subgroup or household outcome is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A stage ratio may reflect timing, category definitions, geography, or differing denominators rather than an approval, referral, payment, or recovery rate; reported aggregate amounts do not prove individual protection.

observations.period: Current API snapshot run October 20, 2026; Los Angeles County wildfire program-stage recheck

denominator.unit: city/ZIP rows returned by the OpenFEMA Registration Intake and Individuals Household Program dataset; aggregate categories are not a unique-survivor longitudinal denominator

valid_registrations.unit: valid registrations reported in the current aggregate snapshot

ihp_referrals.unit: IHP referrals in the current aggregate snapshot

ihp_eligible.unit: IHP-eligible records in the current aggregate snapshot

reported_ihp_amount.unit: U.S. dollars in reported aggregate IHP amounts across housing-assistance and other-needs-assistance fields

snapshot_change.value: Compared with the retained September snapshot, the current run reports 1 more valid registration, 1 more referral, 4 more eligible records, and approximately $2.013 million more in aggregate IHP amount; this is a data-vintage difference, not a person-level payment trajectory

receipt_and_recovery.unit: missing individual award issuance, payment date and receipt, amount adequacy, appeal, repair or housing completion, insurance interaction, stable placement, repeat crisis, trust, and later action

observations.method: Current OpenFEMA API extraction grouped over the 621 returned city/ZIP rows for disaster 4856; field totals are summed from the public aggregate response and are not treated as a person-level funnel.
observations.uncertainty: The API response is aggregate geography-by-program data, not unique applicants followed over time. It does not disclose applicant identity, damage severity, application sequence, duplicate or invalid-record handling, appeal, payment issuance, receipt, or adequacy.
observations.subgroup: Los Angeles County wildfire registration and program-stage aggregates across the returned city/ZIP rows; no survivor-level subgroup or household outcome is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Small changes between API vintages can reflect late reporting, revisions, or category timing rather than newly paid or recovered households; reported aggregate amounts do not prove individual protection.

boundary: This record establishes a disaster-specific administrative sequence from registration through referral, eligibility, current aggregate assistance amount, and a dated API-vintage comparison. It does not establish survivor approval, payment receipt, amount adequacy, repair or housing recovery, trust, political action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the OpenFEMA aggregate API snapshot; survivor identifiers, applications, payment files, and personally identifying information are not retained.
